_comment: Pinned llama.cpp release. Bump deliberately via scripts/update_llama_version.py (future). sha256s are computed by us at pin time (llama.cpp does not publish checksums) -- trust-on-first-download, recorded here for future audits.

notes.macos: Metal acceleration is built into the standard macOS asset -- no separate GPU variant needed.
notes.windows_gpu: windows-x64-cuda / windows-x64-vulkan asset entries can be added the same way when GPU support is validated on Windows; stubbed out in platform_detect.py for now.
notes.linux_arm64_cuda_note: No linux-arm64-cuda asset published upstream at all (Jetson-class boards are the only real-world arm64+CUDA host) -- source_build.py builds llama-server from vendor/llama.cpp instead of falling back to linux-arm64-cpu, which would silently throw away the GPU.
notes.min_glibc: llama.cpp's own release CI builds Linux arm64 assets against a newer base image than most arm64 boards actually run -- confirmed live 2026-09-23: the b10989 linux-arm64-cpu asset needs glibc 2.38 (via its GLIBC_* symbol versions, `objdump -T llama-server | grep GLIBC_`), which JetPack 6.2.3 / Ubuntu 22.04 (glibc 2.35) does not have, so even the CPU-only asset fails to start there (not just the missing CUDA asset). The x64-cpu asset only needs glibc 2.34, so this mostly bites arm64. Not re-verified per release bump -- re-check with the same objdump command whenever `tag` changes, since the CI base image is upstream's choice, not ours.

source_build._comment: Used when platform_detect.resolve_install_strategy (aipotluck/installer/build_strategy.py) decides no viable prebuilt asset exists for this host -- builds llama-server from the pinned tag checked out into vendor/llama.cpp instead. Confirmed viable on a real Jetson Orin Nano (JetPack 6.2.3): a manually-built llama-server there already links libggml-cuda.so against the JetPack-bundled CUDA 12.6 toolkit at CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=87.
source_build.apt_packages_note: libssl-dev is easy to miss and does NOT fail the cmake configure step -- llama.cpp's HTTPS support (LLAMA_OPENSSL, needed for the -hf model downloader and --cache-list our pull/list commands depend on) does a plain, non-REQUIRED find_package(OpenSSL) and silently compiles without HTTPS if the dev headers aren't present, so a build can succeed and only fail later at runtime with 'HTTPS is not supported'. source_build.py checks for the header before ever starting cmake, specifically to avoid burning a 30-90 minute build on a binary with this silently missing.
